1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

We need to build a playable game: "2D Fortnite building inside a Worms artillery match." So a Worms-like turn-based artillery game with destructible terrain plus Fortnite-style 2D building (placing wood/brick/metal structures). Needs to be a static HTML game (index.html) likely with vanilla JS canvas, mobile touch support.

Let me design a solid, polished game.

Concept: "FORTNITE ARTILLERY" — 2D turn-based Worms match. Two teams (player vs AI) on destructible terrain. Each turn you can move (limited fuel), aim & charge a shot, or build structures using materials. Buildings are destructible blocks/walls/ramps/platforms that block projectiles and protect worms. Fortnite building: quick-build pieces (wall, floor, ramp) placed on a grid near your worm, costs materials, instantly builds. Materials harvested from destructible crates/terrain? Could add material pickups.

Key features:
- Procedurally generated destructible terrain using per-pixel bitmask? Canvas pixel manipulation for simplicity. Better: heightmap-based terrain with circular destruction? For Worms feel, pixel destructible terrain is best. Use offscreen canvas terrain mask, destruct with radial brush. Collision via pixel sampling. Rendering beautiful layered terrain using gradient + edge highlight.
- Physics: gravity, wind, bouncing projectiles, explosions.
- Weapons: bazooka, grenade (timed bounce), shotgun? Keep 3: Rocket (straight w/ wind), Grenade (bounce + 3s fuse), Cluster? Maybe "pump shotgun" hitscan short range.
- Building: select Wall / Floor / Ramp. Build points grid snapped to 24px cells near worm. Costs wood 10. Building blocks destructible with HP, can be shot, block shots & worms stand on them.
- Materials: start each worm with 100 wood? Simplify: each team has a shared material pool of 150, harvested by destroying "loot crates" scattered and by terrain destruction? Fortnite vibe: harvesting. Let's implement: each team has wood/brick/metal. Destroying terrain yields wood. But complexity. Simpler: each team starts with 100 wood, gains 10 per turn and 15 per hit? Hmm.

Let's make it manageled: Each turn you get +25 materials automatically, cap 150; destroying crates gives 25. Build pieces cost 25 (wall), 15 (floor), 35 (ramp). Maybe each build type same material cost 20.

- Turn system with 60s timer, wind changes each turn, camera follows projectile, damage numbers, particles, screen shake.
- AI opponent: aims with ballistic computation with some inaccuracy, tries to build a wall if health low? Basic AI: choose weapon, compute trajectory with wind, adjust, fire; sometimes builds wall in front. Needs to be competent but beatable.

- Win condition: eliminate enemy team. 1v1 or 2v2? Let's do 2v2? Might be complex for turn ordering but fine. Simpler and more focused: 1 worm per team? "Worms artillery match" typically team. Let's do teams of 2 with turn order alternating teams, controlling active worm. Health 100 each. Could be good but more code. Player team 2 worms, enemy 2. Turn: player worm 1, enemy worm 1, player worm 2, enemy worm 2, etc. Buildings must not trap the active worm.

Maybe 1v1 for clarity/polish, with "Best of" not needed. But Worms feel with teams. Let's do 2v2 but simple.

Mobile: on-screen touch controls for aim, power, move, jump, build, fire. Need responsive layout. Canvas with fixed virtual resolution scaled to fit, touch buttons in DOM for D-pad etc.

Let me architect:

Single index.html with embedded CSS and modules? Static site can serve multiple JS files. Cleaner: index.html, style.css, game.js (maybe modules pieces). Use plain JS with multiple files? Simpler for robust load: main.js as module plus separate modules. The server serves .js. Use ES modules. Let's split:
- index.html
- styles.css
- src/main.js
- src/terrain.js
- src/entities.js
- src/game.js ... 

But single-file might be easier for capture and less risk. However maintainability matters. I'll do a few modules: `src/game.js` (core loop & states), `src/terrain.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/ai.js`, `src/ui.js`? Overkill. I'll build with 2-3 files.

Visual style: colorful, cartoon Fortnite-ish with purple sky, floating islands, building grid, chunky UI panels. Worms represented as cute characters with helmets. Terrain: layered grass/dirt, destructible. Buildings: wooden planks/brick/metal textures drawn procedurally, with health and damage cracks.

Game loop turn-based with real-time physics while projectile in flight.

Controls:
- Left/right arrows or A/D: move active worm (limited move distance per turn)
- Space or W: jump
- Up/Down: aim angle
- Left/Right? conflict with move. Use mouse aim: drag from worm to aim (mobile friendly). Keyboard: up/down angle, Q/E? Let's design clean:
  - Mouse/touch: click & drag anywhere on battlefield to aim and charge (like Angry Birds), release to fire? But need separate fire/cancel. Drag from worm backwards to set angle/power, release fires. That's intuitive and touch-friendly.
  - Movement: A/D or arrow left/right; jump W/Space; on-screen buttons on mobile.
  - Weapon switch: keys 1/2/3 or weapon chips.
  - Build: B toggles build mode; 1/2/3 chooses wall/floor/ramp; click near worm to place. Mobile: build button then tap.
  - Fire: button "FIRE" uses current aim/power; keyboard Space? Space is jump. Use Enter to fire, or just release drag.
  
Simplify input scheme: aim with mouse position relative to active worm (angle), power via hold? Hmm, drag-to-aim is best. When not dragging, show aim reticle based on mouse hover? For accessibility/keyboard: ArrowUp/Down adjust angle, Left/Right adjust power? But then movement keys conflict.

Standard Worms: Left/Right move, Up/Down aim, Space jump, Enter fire, hold Space to charge. Let's map:
- A/D or ←/→: walk
- W or ↑: aim up; S or ↓: aim down (hold, continuous)
- Space: jump
- Hold Enter (or click "Fire") to charge power, release to fire. Also mouse drag on canvas gives aim+power.
- 1-4 weapons
- B build mode, then 1/2/3 piece, click/tap canvas near worm to place; right click/Esc cancel.

On mobile, DOM controls: left, right, jump, aim up/down, fire (hold), build, weapon selector. Drag directly on canvas also works. That's a lot of buttons but manageable: bottom bar with dpad, jump, aim +/- and fire; top chips for weapons/build.

Given time, I need to be efficient but thorough. Let's plan implementation in detail.

### World
Virtual dimensions 1600x900? Canvas render with DPR scaling; game world coordinates in CSS pixels based on canvas size. Terrain generated based on canvas width/height at start (responsive problem: resizing mid-game). Better use fixed world 1280x720 and letterbox with scaling. On mobile portrait 390x844, fixed 1280x720 scaled to fit width -> small. For mobile, use adaptive world dimensions? Could set world height taller in portrait. Hmm.

Simpler: use fixed logical world 1440x810 (16:9), canvas fills screen with letterbox black. On phone portrait, gameplay would be small. Mobile requirement: usable touch controls and responsive layouts. Many browser games ask rotate device. Could show "rotate for best experience" but still playable. Alternative dynamic world: world width = viewport width / scale, height = viewport height / scale with minimum scale. Terrain generator uses world size. If resize between turns, regenerate? Not ideal.

Approach: canvas internal resolution adapts to available viewport with a zoom factor. World is 1600 wide, 900 tall (base). Camera scales so world visible with letterboxing; on portrait, use a camera that follows the active worm at higher zoom (e.g., scale to width with world width ~1000 visible), and allow panning? Complexity.

Keep it simple and robust: canvas covers full viewport, world coordinates = CSS pixels of canvas; on resize, we recompute terrain? We can generate terrain at initial load and if aspect ratio changes drastically, use "scale transform" from design resolution 1280x720 to canvas with cover/contain. Let's use design resolution 1280x720 and scale with `Math.min(cw/1280, ch/720)`, center; for portrait, that leaves lots of vertical space for touch controls below? Actually canvas element can be sized to available area above controls, then contain scale, leaving letterbox. Touch controls live in a fixed bottom overlay; gameplay area is above. On 390x844 with controls 220px, canvas 390x624: scale = min(390/1280, 624/720)=0.305, world appears tiny (390x219 within 624 tall). Bad.

Therefore mobile portrait: recommend landscape, but still implement touch controls for portrait with a camera zoomed out and UI. Many artillery games need wide view. Terrain and gameplay could work with a more vertical map! Two teams on either side, vertical space used for high terrain and building. Portrait aspect 0.6 => world 720x1200. Two worms separated horizontally ~600 px, still fine with smaller sprites. Camera fit width. This suggests dynamic world dimensions: maintain area aspect and generate terrain based on it, with min width 800. On desktop 1440x900 aspect 1.6 -> world 1440x900. On mobile portrait 390x624 aspect 0.625 -> world 800x1280? Then worms at x=120 and x=680, terrain height variable. Weapon ranges adapt. Maybe use a responsive world with width/height computed, and design flexible terrain. I'll add a graceful portrait experience: show overlay with rotate icon and a "Play anyway" link that uses a camera system? Hmm.

Let's prioritize a great desktop game with mobile support via landscape recommendation + functional portrait (canvas letterboxed but controls work, plus pinch? ). ## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D browser game combining Fortnite-style building with a Worms-style turn-based artillery match, starting from an empty repo.

## Requirements
- Build immediately without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them.
- Playable game with destructible terrain, building, artillery, and AI opponent.
- Support Android/iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Static deployment via `index.html` (repo has no package.json).

## Decisions
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/ES modules + Canvas 2D, no external dependencies or assets.
- 2v2 turn-based artillery: player squad vs AI rivals, alternating worm turns.
- 3 weapons: RPG (infinite), Grenade (3 each), Cluster (2 each); shiftable wind.
- Fortnite-style quick-build: Wall, Floor, Ramp; destructible, 4 builds/turn, shared wood materials, grid-snapped near active worm.
- Loot llamas grant +50 wood when destroyed; destructible terrain via canvas + analytic collision mask.
- AI chooses shots by simulating candidate trajectories with wind/terrain/buildings, with aim error for fairness.
- Responsive camera: full battlefield on desktop/landscape; portrait uses zoomed camera following the action.
- Procedural WebAudio sound (no external files).
- Pause render loop on menu so automated `Play` click is reliable.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full project scaffold: `index.html`, `css/style.css`, all JS modules.
- Implemented terrain generation/destruction, worm movement/physics, buildings, weapons, explosions, llamas, particles, wind, camera, AI, turn flow, win/lose, HUD, start/result screens, touch/keyboard/mouse controls.
- Added sound synthesis and mute toggle.
- Added safety: auto-start capture button has `aria-label="Play"`.
- Verified all JS files pass `node --check`.
- Dev server successfully running on `http://localhost:3002` in tmux session `fortgame`.
- Start screen renders and looks good in desktop screenshot (`screenshots/final-desktop.png`).
- Real mouse click starts game correctly (`state: 'aim'`, worms spawned at expected positions).
- Optimized terrain generation from ~5.6s to ~65–80ms by replacing `getImageData` readback with analytic mask construction (`terrain.buildMask`).
- Cached static sky, world background, and vignette layers (`Game.ensureCaches`); merged scorch rendering into main terrain canvas.
- Menu render loop now stops after first frame.

### Active
- Performance investigation under Playwright SwiftShader/software rendering.
- Latest measurements: menu FPS ~3.1 (paused), game FPS with HUD hidden ~0.75–3.4, full render flush 130–357ms.
- Confusing latest result: “game fps hud shown 31.58” after toggling HUD back on — likely measurement/render-loop artifact; needs re-verification.
- Initial automated capture still failed because `page.click` timed out; force click succeeded but post-click `page.evaluate` took ~11s due to rendering blocking.

### Blocked
- Capture reliability: `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3002 CAPTURE_DIR=screenshots ./capture.sh` previously failed with “auto-start not-actionable” / `TimeoutError` during Play click.
- Gameplay performance on software rendering likely too slow for smooth capture/gameplay; needs further optimization and retest.

## Next Move
1. Re-run `./capture.sh` now that menu pauses and caches exist, with env vars set; inspect both screenshots.
2. Measure FPS/hud impact more reliably (start game, wait for idle, then evaluate RAF counter) and identify remaining rendering hotspot.
3. Reduce render cost: lower internal canvas resolution / cap pixel count, reduce aim-preview dots, pre-render worm sprites, remove or reduce HUD `backdrop-filter` and large gradients/shadows.
4. Verify gameplay manually via browser: movement, jump, aiming, weapon switching, firing, building placement, AI turn, explosions, llamas, game over/play again.
5. Fix any gameplay logic bugs found (e.g., grenade preview bounce condition in `physics.simulateTrajectory`, destroyed building particles, AI building/aim behavior).
6. Run final capture on desktop + mobile and confirm no console errors, non-blank game screens.
7. Update README with game description/controls if time allows.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: app markup, start/HUD/result screens, touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: full visual design, responsive HUD, animations; potential perf-heavy backdrop-filters.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js`: main `Game` class, setup/turn/update/input/UI/render/caches.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/physics.js`: collision, support, walking, placement validation, trajectory simulation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/actions.js`: firing, projectile stepping, explosions, damage, llamas.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/terrain.js`: procedural destructible terrain + analytic mask (optimized).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/visuals.js`: sky/background/worm/building/llama/particle/aim rendering.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/ai.js`: AI shot planning/build decisions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/build.js`: quick-build placement.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/config.js`: constants, weapons, builds, teams.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/effects.js`: particles/text effects.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: WebAudio synth.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/utils.js`: math/helpers.
- `/tmp/opencode/inspect.cjs`, `/tmp/opencode/clicktest*.cjs`, `/tmp/opencode/fps*.cjs`, `/tmp/opencode/perf.cjs`: diagnostic Playwright scripts using runtime config.

## Important Context
- Server: `tmux new-session -d -s fortgame 'PORT=3002 ./start.sh'`, logs via `tmux capture-pane -pt fortgame`.
- Capture command: `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3002 CAPTURE_DIR=screenshots ./capture.sh`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D browser game combining Fortnite-style building with a Worms-style turn-based artillery match, starting from an empty repo.

## Requirements
- Build immediately without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them.
- Playable game with destructible terrain, building, artillery, and AI opponent.
- Support Android/iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Static deployment via `index.html` (repo has no package.json).

## Decisions
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/ES modules + Canvas 2D, no external dependencies or assets.
- 2v2 turn-based artillery: player squad vs AI rivals, alternating worm turns.
- 3 weapons: RPG (infinite), Grenade (3 each), Cluster (2 each); shiftable wind.
- Fortnite-style quick-build: Wall, Floor, Ramp; destructible, 4 builds/turn, shared wood materials, grid-snapped near active worm.
- Loot llamas grant +50 wood when destroyed; destructible terrain via canvas + analytic collision mask.
- AI simulates candidate trajectories with wind/terrain/buildings, with aim error for fairness.
- Responsive camera: full battlefield on desktop/landscape; portrait uses zoomed camera following the action.
- Procedural WebAudio sound (no external files).
- Capture reliability: keep a cheap menu rAF loop, but do not render the battlefield until the match starts.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full game implemented: terrain generation/destruction, worms, physics, buildings, weapons, projectiles, explosions, llamas, particles, wind, camera, AI, turn flow, win/lose, HUD, start/result screens, touch/keyboard/mouse controls, sound and mute.
- Fixed capture blocker: `./capture.sh` now reports `auto-start clicked` for desktop and mobile (~8s total).
- Root cause of stalled frames/capture: terrain’s 1500×900 offscreen canvas was GPU-backed. Using `getContext('2d', { willReadFrequently: true })` for terrain plus sky/world/vignette caches made frames flow and trial clicks complete quickly.
- Removed performance-heavy CSS: full-screen `backdrop-filter`, HUD/dock/palette/pill blur, `text-wrap: balance`, animated start glow, start-glow blur filter.
- Removed unused `terrain.scars` canvas.
- Menu no longer renders the battlefield; cheap rAF keeps input/capture responsive.
- Fixed stale-view camera bug: `computeView()` now runs before initial camera setup and in `startMatch`; `startTurn` uses `updateCamera(0, first)`.
- Moved floating islands higher/away from spawns; worms now spawn on main terrain via `terrain.surfaceBelow(x, H * 0.35, H)` instead of on islands.
- Default 45°/60% shot now travels across the map and lands near the rival (≈x1357, y606).
- Aim preview dots enlarged/brightened.
- Grenade preview now bounces off buildings as well as terrain.
- Destroyed buildings now emit debris via `burstBuild`.
- Rotate hint moved to top (`calc(120px + var(--safe-t))`) so it no longer covers the dock; HUD bottom padding increased to 12px.
- Captured desktop/mobile gameplay screenshots show full battlefield, HUD, aim arc, llamas, and portrait target chip.
- Logic test: start, movement, jump, build placement, firing, projectile/settle, AI turn, and return to player all work with no page errors.

### Active
- Final gameplay verification after the latest `makeWorm` and HUD padding changes.
- Need to re-run capture and inspect desktop/mobile screenshots with worms on the ground and the rotate hint repositioned.
- Verify win/lose/play-again, AI damage output, llama loot with mats below cap, grenade bounce, building destruction, and weapon ammo switching.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check` on all `js/*.js` files.
2. Re-run `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3002 CAPTURE_DIR=screenshots ./capture.sh`; inspect both screenshots for ground spawns, aim preview, dock fit, and rotate-hint placement.
3. Extend `/tmp/opencode/logic.cjs` to test win/lose/play again, AI hits, llama loot with mats below 180, grenade bounces, and destructible buildings.
4. Fix any bugs found.
5. Update `README.md` with game description, controls, and assumptions.
6. Run a final capture and confirm no console errors and non-blank game screens.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js`: main loop, menu/capture behavior, camera, turns, HUD, input, render/caches.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: responsive UI, start screen, HUD/dock, rotate hint.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/terrain.js`: destructible terrain, analytic mask, floating island placement, CPU-rasterized canvas.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/physics.js`: collision, support, movement, placement validation, trajectory simulation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/actions.js`: weapons, projectiles, explosions, damage, llama loot, building debris.

# Fort Artillery

A playable 2D browser game that mashes up **Fortnite-style quick building** with a **Worms-style turn-based artillery duel**. Two squads of worms trade shots across a destructible battlefield while wind, terrain, and player-built forts decide who survives.

Built with plain HTML, CSS, Canvas 2D, and ES modules. No dependencies, no build step, no external assets.

## Play

Open `index.html` through any static web server:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
# then visit http://localhost:8000
```

The game also works when hosted from a static path such as GitHub Pages.

## How to play

- **2v2, alternating turns.** Each squad has two worms. Eliminate both rivals to win.
- **Move** with `A` / `D` or the on-screen arrows. Each turn has a 140 px movement budget.
- **Jump** with `Space` or the **JUMP** button.
- **Aim** with `↑` / `↓`, drag directly on the battlefield, or use the direction buttons.
- **Fire** with `Enter`, the **FIRE!** button, or by releasing a drag.
- **Build** with `B`, then tap/click the map. Choose **Wall**, **Floor**, or **Ramp**.
  - Up to 4 pieces per turn, placed on a 72 px grid near the active worm.
  - Walls and ramps cost 20/25 wood, floors cost 15. Each team starts with 100 wood and gains 28 at the start of its turn (cap 180).
- **Loot llamas** by destroying them for +50 wood.
- **Wind** pushes projectiles sideways and changes every turn. Watch the arrow in the top bar.

### Weapons

| Weapon | Ammo | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RPG | Infinite | Fast, reliable arc. Good for direct hits. |
| Grenade | 3 per worm | Bounces off terrain and buildings, then explodes on its fuse. |
| Cluster | 2 per worm | Splits into three bomblets on impact. |

### Touch and mobile

- Every action has an on-screen control; keyboard shortcuts are optional.
- The HUD, weapon dock, and safe areas adapt to phones and tablets in portrait and landscape.
- In portrait the camera follows the active worm. A target chip points toward an off-screen rival.
- A dismissible rotate hint suggests landscape for the widest view.

## Features

- Procedurally generated destructible terrain with explosion craters.
- Destructible player and AI buildings, with debris and hit feedback.
- Projectile physics with wind, gravity, bouncing, fuses, and cluster splits.
- AI opponents that build defensively, simulate trajectories, account for wind and cover, and aim with a human-like error margin.
- Camera that frames the whole battlefield in landscape and follows the action in portrait.
- Procedural WebAudio sound effects and a mute toggle.
- Captured with headless Chromium on desktop and mobile viewports as part of the development checks.

## Project layout

```
index.html          markup, HUD, start/result screens
css/style.css       responsive layout, HUD, dock, overlays
js/main.js          boot and diagnostics hook
js/game.js          main loop, turns, camera, input, HUD, render caches
js/config.js        weapons, builds, teams, tuning constants
js/terrain.js       destructible terrain and collision mask
js/physics.js       movement, collision, placement, trajectory preview
js/actions.js       firing, projectiles, explosions, damage, loot
js/build.js         quick-build placement and material costs
js/ai.js            rival building and shot planning
js/visuals.js       world, worms, buildings, llamas, aim rendering
js/effects.js       particles and floating combat text
js/audio.js         procedural sound
```

## Assumptions

- Single-player local match: one human squad versus one AI squad.
- Fixed 2v2 rosters and three weapons keep matches short and readable on phones.
- Quick-build is intentionally limited to four grid-snapped pieces per turn near the active worm, so it complements artillery instead of replacing it.
- No persistence or networking; every match starts with a fresh battlefield, wind, and full health/ammo.
